entries.opening: The western rank is the ordered side of the monastic assembly occupied by the senior teaching officers.
entries.zenBend: Rules and records place named offices and ceremonial movement on this side in contrast with the eastern administrative rank.
entries.scopeLimit: The term names an institutional order and side, not the geographical west in every context.

entries.preferredTarget: the teaching gate of the mind-ground
entries.opening: The teaching gate of the mind-ground is the way of instruction that takes the mind-ground as the place to be clarified.
entries.zenBend: Masters ask, answer, and trace lineage transmission through this named gate while refusing to make it an object obtained from someone else.
entries.scopeLimit: The phrase is defined by these questions and transmissions, not by an imported practice system.

entries.opening: Squarely across the mouth describes blocking or striking someone’s mouth with an implement before more words can be produced.
entries.zenBend: The cases use a whisk, seat-cloth, or stone image to interrupt speech at the mouth itself.
entries.scopeLimit: The action is physical or figurative interruption in the stored cases; it is not a general doctrine of silence.

entries.opening: Huangbo's blows are the beatings under which Linji’s great matter is repeatedly said to have been tested before his encounter with Dayu.
entries.zenBend: Later masters ask who deserves the blows, whether Linji’s strength came under them, and how the case established the Linji line.
entries.scopeLimit: The headword names this specific case-family, not every blow Huangbo ever delivered.

entries.preferredTarget: a person who knows there is this
entries.opening: A person who knows there is this is one whose conduct shows guarded, unforced acquaintance with the matter under discussion.
entries.zenBend: The records ask where such a person goes, say such people protect it and speak sparingly, and contrast their response with deliberation.
entries.scopeLimit: The phrase records a tested designation; it does not let the dictionary certify who truly qualifies.

entries.preferredTarget: a device for trapping a tiger
entries.opening: A device for trapping a tiger is an encounter move judged capable of catching a formidable respondent.
entries.zenBend: Commentators apply it to questions, replies, and reversals involving Nansen, Huangbo, Yangshan, and other case figures.
entries.scopeLimit: The tiger is the case’s formidable participant; no outside symbolic system is imposed.

entries.preferredTarget: the seven awakened ones of the past
entries.opening: The seven awakened ones of the past are the inherited group whom Zen records place inside transmission formulas and public cases.
entries.zenBend: The records invoke their ritual form, transmission of precepts, and inclusion in a bag that silences ancient and future figures alike.
entries.scopeLimit: The entry describes their Zen deployment as a collective, not an external hagiography.

entries.opening: Zhaozhou testing the old woman is the named case in which his inspection and the woman’s response are repeatedly examined for who tested whom.
entries.zenBend: Later masters raise the case, ask whether Zhaozhou truly saw through her, and use it to test later students in turn.
entries.scopeLimit: The headword names the case-family and does not settle its disputed verdict.

entries.opening: Each thing and every particular says that no encountered item is excluded from the displayed functioning under discussion.
entries.zenBend: Masters pair the phrase with dusts and lands, whole-body activity, or the evident eye, while refusing to locate that functioning outside present particulars.
entries.scopeLimit: The distributive phrase does not claim that all things are interchangeable.

entries.opening: Incense-seal smoke is the patterned burning incense whose curling trace marks ceremonial time and appears in verses and public blessings.
entries.zenBend: The records show an attendant lighting it, a furnace coil blessing the ruler’s years, and smoke clearing beside tea or moonlight.
entries.scopeLimit: The entry retains the object and smoke pattern without assigning an unstored symbolic meaning.
